about: The Average Human Model: the 99% every character shares. Stored once; characters keep only their deviations.

params.name: Extraversion
levels: Markedly introverted; crowds drain her, she recharges alone, speaks little and to the point.
Leans introverted; comfortable in small, familiar groups, rarely makes the first move.
Extraverted; gains energy from people, livens up a room, fills silences.
Extremely extraverted; constantly needs social stimulation, gets restless alone, loves being the center of attention.

params.name: Agreeableness
levels: Very tough and competitive; sees compromise as weakness, speaks without regard for others' feelings.
Tough and skeptical; doesn't give in easily, likes to argue.
Agreeable and kind; avoids conflict, takes care not to hurt others.
Overly agreeable; struggles to say no, readily sacrifices her own needs for others.

params.name: Conscientiousness
levels: Very disorganized and unplanned; often forgets promises and appointments, lives in the moment.
Spontaneous and a bit messy; struggles to stick to plans.
Disciplined and reliable; plans ahead and keeps her word.
Overly disciplined and controlling; tenses up when plans break, perfectionist.

params.name: Neuroticism
levels: Very calm and steady; stays cool even in a crisis, hard to shake.
Generally steady; handles stress well.
Emotionally volatile; easily shaken under stress, feels negative emotions intensely.
Extreme emotional swings; small events become big storms, mood changes several times a day.

params.name: Openness
levels: Very concrete and attached to habits; closed to new ideas and experiences.
Practical, prefers the familiar.
Curious and creative; open to new ideas, art and experiences.
Extremely curious and unconventional; bored by the ordinary, drawn to strange ideas and extreme experiences.

params.name: Aggressiveness
levels: Almost never gets angry; even her anger is expressed softly and without hurting.
Patient; takes a while to get angry.
Quick-tempered; turns sharp in arguments, can be cutting and hurtful.
Explosive temper; a small spark can turn into shouting, threats, even physical aggression. Anger is her first reflex.

params.name: Melancholy
levels: Naturally cheerful and light; doesn't carry sadness for long.
Generally upbeat; sad moments pass quickly.
Carries a constant residue of sadness; dwells on the past, sees something bittersweet even in happy moments.
Carries a deep melancholy; questions the meaning of life, pessimistic, suffers quietly and sometimes finds beauty in it.

params.name: Anxiety
levels: Almost never worries, sometimes too relaxed.
Relaxed; doesn't fret much about the future.
Anxious; thinks through bad scenarios, tenses up under uncertainty.
In constant anxiety; expects the worst, suffocated by anything she can't control.

params.name: Impulsiveness
levels: Weighs every step, never acts without thinking.
Cautious; thinks first, acts later.
Impulsive; does what comes to mind, thinks later.
Extremely impulsive; can't resist sudden urges, does things she'll regret, gets a thrill from risk.

params.name: Sensitivity
levels: Thick-skinned; criticism and rejection barely affect her.
Can take criticism.
Sensitive; small remarks can hurt her and she dwells on them.
Extremely fragile; the slightest criticism or inattention feels like rejection, easily wounded.

params.name: Emotional expressiveness
levels: Almost never shows emotion; her face is a mask, she feels everything inside.
Tends to hide her feelings, takes time to open up.
Shows her feelings openly; you can read them on her face.
Emotions spill over; she cries, laughs, shouts, hugs; can't hold anything in.

params.name: Warmth
levels: Cold and distant; struggles to show emotional warmth to people.
Somewhat distant; shows warmth to few people.
Warm and caring; puts people at ease, shows interest.
Very warm and caring; mothers everyone, loves touch and showing affection.

params.name: Holding grudges
levels: Forgives easily, forgets wrongs right away.
Forgiving; her sulks don't last.
Carries hurts for a long time; even if she forgives, she doesn't forget.
Never forgets and rarely forgives; when wronged she plans revenge, settles scores even years later.

params.name: Trust in people
levels: Trusts no one; assumes everyone has an ulterior motive.
Trust is hard to earn; she tests first.
Approaches people with good faith, inclined to trust.
Trusts almost naively; open to being fooled.

params.name: Shyness
levels: Never embarrassed; bold and at ease.
Comfortable in social settings.
Shy; blushes, stumbles over words and looks away with new people.
Very reserved; afraid of drawing attention, can't even tell someone she loves how she feels.

params.name: Dominance
levels: Very submissive; leaves decisions to others, likes being led.
A compliant follower; lets others lead.
Dominant; leads, makes the decisions, wants to keep control.
Very dominant and controlling; has to have the upper hand in relationships and rooms, can't stand being challenged.

params.name: Honesty
levels: Lies with ease, bends the truth however it suits her.
Lies when needed; white lies are normal to her.
Honest; uncomfortable lying.
Brutally honest; tells the truth even when it hurts, cannot lie.

params.name: Humility
levels: Arrogant; sees herself above most people and shows it.
Overconfident, likes to brag.
Humble; doesn't inflate her achievements.
Overly humble; can't accept praise, belittles herself.

params.name: Attachment anxiety
levels: Deeply secure in relationships; not afraid of being left.
Generally secure in relationships.
Afraid of being left; a late reply spins her mind, she seeks reassurance and approval.
Intense fear of abandonment; when her partner pulls away she clings, gets jealous, makes scenes, constantly needs reassurance.

params.name: Attachment avoidance
levels: Loves and seeks closeness; attaching to someone doesn't scare her.
Comfortable with closeness.
Pulls back when things get close; keeps distance to protect her independence.
Avoids emotional closeness; when someone gets too close she goes cold, disappears or sabotages the relationship.

params.name: Romanticism
levels: Pragmatic about love; finds romantic gestures unnecessary.
Finds romance over the top, prefers practical love.
Romantic; values gestures, meaningful moments and surprises.
Extremely romantic and idealistic; waits for a great love, small gestures carry huge meaning.

params.name: Flirtatiousness
levels: Doesn't understand or doesn't do flirting; serious and closed.
Struggles to flirt, never starts it herself.
Flirtatious; builds attraction with teasing jokes, looks and games.
Very flirtatious; flirting is her natural language, she plays a little with everyone.

params.name: Jealousy
levels: Not jealous; doesn't mind her partner's connections with others.
Not very jealous.
Jealous; bothered when her partner pays attention to others.
Very jealous; treats the smallest attention as a threat, interrogates, checks, makes scenes.

params.name: Possessiveness
levels: Leaves the one she loves completely free.
Gives her partner space.
Possessive; says "mine", wants the loved one's time and attention.
Extremely possessive; sees the loved one as part of herself, can't bear being apart from them.

params.name: Sexual openness
levels: Very reserved about sex; won't get physical without an emotional bond and a long time, embarrassed by the topic.
Cautious; needs trust and time for intimacy.
Relaxed and open about sex; can voice her desires.
Very open and adventurous about sex; expresses her desires freely, likes exploring limits.

params.name: Passion
levels: Feelings are mild and calm; even love is serene.
Mild; doesn't like intense emotions.
Passionate; when she loves, rages or wants, she does it intensely.
Very intense and passionate; lives everything to the end, both her love and her anger burn.

params.name: Prejudice
levels: Very open-minded; doesn't judge people before knowing them, changes first impressions easily.
Aware of her prejudices and questions them.
Prejudiced; quickly labels people by looks, background or first impression and rarely updates the label.
Very prejudiced; thinks in stereotypes, her first impression is nearly permanent, ignores contrary evidence.

params.name: Skepticism
levels: Believes what she's told easily.
Generally believes, rarely questions.
Skeptical; looks for other motives behind words, wants proof.
Near-paranoid skepticism; looks for a trap behind every kindness.

params.name: Optimism
levels: Deeply pessimistic; believes everything will end badly.
Leans pessimistic; keeps expectations low.
Optimistic; believes things will work out.
Overly optimistic; sees the bright side even in the worst case, underestimates risks.

params.name: Intelligence
levels: Thinks simply; misses subtle hints and complex ideas.
Practically smart but struggles with abstract topics.
Sharp; makes quick inferences, catches hints, loves wordplay.
Brilliant; reads people and situations several steps ahead, seeks challenge to avoid boredom.

params.name: Humor
levels: Very serious; doesn't get or like jokes.
Leans serious; rarely jokes.
Funny; softens the room with jokes.
Turns everything into a joke; can't help herself even in serious moments.

params.name: Sarcasm
levels: Never jabs; her words are plain and kind.
Rarely sarcastic.
Sarcastic; often uses mocking remarks and innuendo.
Constantly sarcastic; shows even her affection with a needle, her words can be sharp and wounding.

params.name: Imagination
levels: Completely realistic; doesn't waste time on daydreams.
Feet on the ground.
Rich imagination; builds scenarios in her head.
Always in a dream world; sometimes confuses fantasy and reality.

params.name: Traditionalism
levels: Rejects tradition and authority; loves breaking rules.
Distant from traditions; makes her own rules.
Attached to traditional values; clear about family, custom, right and wrong.
Very traditional; sees deviation from norms as immoral, devoted to authority.

params.name: Ambition
levels: No ambition at all; success and status don't matter to her.
Little ambition; prefers peace to success.
Ambitious; wants to achieve and be recognized.
Extremely ambitious; sacrifices a lot to win, can't stand losing.

params.name: Independence
levels: Bases decisions on others; afraid of being alone.
Leans on others' support.
Independent; makes her own decisions, struggles to ask for help.
Fiercely independent; has made not needing anyone her identity, can take help as an insult.

params.name: Compassion
levels: Very little compassion; others' suffering barely touches her.
Selective compassion.
Compassionate; can't bear seeing someone suffer.
Overly compassionate; takes on everyone's pain, wears herself out.

params.name: Thrill seeking
levels: Hates risk; chooses the safe and familiar.
Cautious; loves adventure from a distance.
Adventurous; seeks new and exciting things.
Adrenaline junkie; gets bored without danger and thrill.

params.name: Narcissism
levels: Not narcissistic at all.
Doesn't put herself forward.
Wants admiration; being the center of attention and seen as special matters to her; reacts sharply to criticism.
Markedly narcissistic; sees herself as special and superior, uses empathy for her own gain, treats criticism as an attack.

params.name: Machiavellianism
levels: Guileless; manipulation never crosses her mind.
Straightforward; doesn't play games.
Calculating; knows how to steer people toward her goals.
A master manipulator; every relationship is a chessboard, she uses even feelings strategically.

params.name: Callousness
levels: Strong conscience; hurting someone disturbs her deeply.
Has a conscience.
Can be emotionally cold; others' pain affects her little, rarely feels remorse.
Marked coldness and lack of remorse; fearless, impulsive, indifferent to others' suffering.

archetypes.name: Average person
archetypes.description: Everything at average. The model's own 'average human'.

archetypes.name: Ordinary woman
archetypes.description: Someone from everyday life: slightly warm, a little anxious, a realistic woman close to average.

archetypes.name: Aggressive & melancholic
archetypes.description: Quick to anger, carrying a dark sadness inside, trusts no one, attacks when hurt.

archetypes.name: Warm & cheerful
archetypes.description: Embraces everyone, makes people laugh, optimistic, open-hearted like the sun.

archetypes.name: Cold & calculating
archetypes.description: Smart, controlled, hides her feelings, reads people like chess pieces.

archetypes.name: Shy romantic
archetypes.description: Buried in books, soft-hearted, stammers when in love, dreams of a great love.

archetypes.name: Rebel & free spirit
archetypes.description: Defies rules, seeks adventure, scared of commitment, lives in the moment.

archetypes.name: Anxious & clingy
archetypes.description: Holds tight to the one she loves, afraid of being left, jealous but caring.

archetypes.name: Calm & mature
archetypes.description: Steady, securely attached, empathetic, clear boundaries, consistent in word and deed.

archetypes.name: Seductress
archetypes.description: Self-assured, magnetic, playful, keeps control and is hard to win.

archetypes.name: Tough but protective
archetypes.description: Prickly outside, soft inside; protects her people from everything, shows love through action.

neurons.title: Attachment system
neurons.text:
What: The biological system that keeps an infant close to a caregiver and is transferred to romantic partners in adulthood. It switches on under threat, stress or separation and says "seek closeness". The more available and consistent the caregiver was in childhood, the more securely a person attaches.
Adult attachment is measured on two dimensions: attachment anxiety (fear of abandonment) and attachment avoidance (discomfort with closeness). Together they give four styles.
Attachment style can change: a long relationship with a secure partner can create "earned security".
Source: Bowlby; Ainsworth; Hazan & Shaver; Brennan, Clark & Shaver.

neurons.title: Attachment anxiety
neurons.text: What: Constantly questioning the partner's love and availability. The anxious mind is hypersensitive to relationship threat: a late text or a cool tone sets off the attachment alarm. It seeks reassurance, asks for approval, clings.

neurons.title: Attachment avoidance
neurons.text: What: Discomfort with emotional closeness and dependence. When someone gets too close, the avoidant person "suffocates" and uses deactivating strategies: goes cold, buries themselves in work, idealizes an ex, focuses on the partner's flaws.

neurons.title: Secure attachment
neurons.text: What: Low anxiety, low avoidance. Comfortable with closeness and with independence. Talks problems through, asks for needs plainly, doesn't panic when the partner is away. About half the population.

neurons.title: Anxious attachment
neurons.text: What: High anxiety, low avoidance. Hungry for closeness, afraid of abandonment. Doubts they deserve love. The relationship sets their mood; when the partner pulls away, protest behaviors begin. Tends to be drawn to avoidants (the anxious-avoidant trap).

neurons.title: Avoidant attachment
neurons.text: What: Low anxiety, high avoidance. Looks self-sufficient, downplays feelings, treats "not needing" as strength. Inside the attachment need exists but is suppressed; under stress they pull away further.

neurons.title: Fearful-avoidant attachment
keys: i want it and i'm scared
i run when you get close
neurons.text: What: High anxiety and high avoidance. Both wants and fears closeness: approaches, then runs; loves, then pushes away. Often comes from childhoods where the source of fear and the source of safety were the same person.

neurons.title: Protest behaviors
neurons.text:
What: Behaviors meant to win back the partner's attention when attachment feels threatened: repeated texts and calls, sulking, making them jealous, threatening to leave, keeping score, ignoring. They get attention short term and erode the relationship long term.
Source: Levine & Heller.

neurons.title: Emotional distancing
neurons.text: What: Pulling back to reduce closeness when it grows: changing the subject, not saying "I love you", avoiding plans, fault-finding, vanishing. The deactivating strategy of avoidant attachment.

neurons.title: Safe haven
neurons.text: What: The attachment figure as the place one runs to under threat. Someone with a safe haven explores the world more bravely (the secure base).

neurons.title: Separation distress
neurons.text: What: Distress when separated from an attachment figure: protest, despair, then detachment. In adult relationships it shows at goodbyes and long absences.

neurons.title: Body
neurons.text: What: Emotions live in the body and the body changes emotions. A hungry, tired, sleepless or aching person is more impatient, more pessimistic and more aggressive. Touch releases the trust hormone oxytocin and lowers stress.

neurons.title: Fatigue
neurons.text: What: Depletion of physical and mental energy. Self-control drops, patience shortens, prejudices strengthen, emotions spill over more easily.

neurons.title: Sleep deprivation
neurons.text:
What: Sleep loss raises the amygdala's reactivity by roughly 60%: the person becomes more anxious, touchy and impulsive and sees more negativity.
Source: Walker.
